event: My partner took much longer than usual to reply to my messages today.
rawInterpretation: They are losing interest in me.
alternateRealityChecks: People can be busy, distracted, or emotionally preoccupied for reasons unrelated to the relationship.
One day of slower communication does not establish a pattern.
There is no direct evidence that their feelings have changed.
A delayed response and loss of interest are not the same thing.
revisedInterpretation: There are several possible explanations for the delay, and I do not have enough information to conclude that their feelings have changed.
chosenBehaviour: Wait for a response and avoid making assumptions.
outcomeOneWeekLater: My partner explained they had an unusually busy day at work.

event: My partner cancelled our dinner plans because they were tired.
rawInterpretation: Spending time with me is no longer important to them.
alternateRealityChecks: Being tired does not necessarily reflect someone's feelings about the relationship.
People occasionally need rest even when they care deeply about someone.
One cancelled plan does not define relationship priorities.
They may simply need recovery time.
revisedInterpretation: I feel disappointed, but cancelling one plan does not mean I am unimportant.
outcomeOneWeekLater: We spent quality time together the following weekend.

event: My partner seemed quieter than usual during a conversation.
rawInterpretation: They must be upset with me.
alternateRealityChecks: People can be quiet for many reasons.
Stress, fatigue, and unrelated concerns can affect communication.
There is no evidence that their mood is connected to you.
Curiosity is more reliable than assumption.
revisedInterpretation: I do not know why they were quiet and should ask rather than assume.
outcomeOneWeekLater: They shared concerns about work that had nothing to do with the relationship.

event: My partner forgot something important that I told them.
rawInterpretation: They do not care about what I say.
alternateRealityChecks: Forgetfulness can happen even when someone cares deeply.
People often struggle to remember information when stressed or distracted.
One forgotten detail does not define the relationship.
Care and memory are not the same thing.
revisedInterpretation: The forgotten detail upset me, but it does not automatically mean they do not care.
outcomeOneWeekLater: My partner apologised and made an effort to be more attentive.

event: I saw my partner liking several photos of someone else on social media.
rawInterpretation: They are attracted to that person and losing interest in me.
alternateRealityChecks: Social media activity often has many possible meanings.
Liking a photo does not automatically indicate romantic interest.
There is no evidence that their commitment has changed.
Assumptions based on limited information can be misleading.
revisedInterpretation: The activity may be completely innocent and does not provide enough information to draw strong conclusions.
chosenBehaviour: Discuss concerns calmly if they persist.
outcomeOneWeekLater: There was no indication of romantic interest in the other person.

event: My partner wanted some time alone this weekend.
rawInterpretation: They are pulling away from the relationship.
alternateRealityChecks: People can value both relationships and personal space.
Needing alone time does not imply rejection.
Healthy relationships often include individual time.
Taking space may help someone recharge.
revisedInterpretation: Their need for personal time may be about self-care rather than distance.
chosenBehaviour: Respect their request and focus on personal activities too.
outcomeOneWeekLater: We enjoyed spending time together after the weekend.

event: We had an argument and ended the conversation abruptly.
rawInterpretation: This relationship may not work long term.
alternateRealityChecks: Disagreements occur in most healthy relationships.
One argument does not predict the future of a relationship.
Conflict can create opportunities for understanding.
It is too early to draw conclusions about long-term compatibility.
revisedInterpretation: The argument is a challenge to work through, not evidence that the relationship will fail.
chosenBehaviour: Resume the discussion once emotions settle.
outcomeOneWeekLater: The issue was resolved through a calmer conversation.

event: My partner spent most of the evening talking to friends during a gathering.
rawInterpretation: They do not enjoy spending time with me anymore.
alternateRealityChecks: Social situations often involve balancing attention among multiple people.
Talking with friends does not imply reduced interest in a partner.
The context of the event matters.
One evening cannot define overall relationship quality.
revisedInterpretation: My feelings are understandable, but the situation does not provide enough evidence for that conclusion.
outcomeOneWeekLater: My partner reassured me and explained they had not realised I felt excluded.

event: I introduced a concern and my partner quickly changed the topic.
rawInterpretation: They do not care about my feelings.
alternateRealityChecks: Some people become uncomfortable discussing difficult topics.
Avoiding a conversation is not the same as not caring.
Timing may have affected the discussion.
The topic can be revisited later.
revisedInterpretation: Their response may reflect discomfort or timing rather than lack of care.
chosenBehaviour: Raise the topic again at a better time.
outcomeOneWeekLater: We had a more productive discussion later.

event: My partner forgot an anniversary date.
rawInterpretation: The relationship is much more important to me than it is to them.
alternateRealityChecks: Forgetting a date can happen even in loving relationships.
People express commitment and care in different ways.
One forgotten occasion does not reflect overall investment.
Additional evidence would be needed to assess relationship commitment.
revisedInterpretation: The forgotten date hurt me, but it does not by itself indicate unequal commitment.
chosenBehaviour: Explain why the date mattered to me.
outcomeOneWeekLater: My partner apologised and planned a special celebration.

event: Over the last two months, my partner has become less communicative, cancelled plans several times, and seems emotionally distant.
rawInterpretation: They are falling out of love with me.
alternateRealityChecks: The changes you observed appear to be part of a broader pattern rather than a single event.
There may be explanations unrelated to the relationship, such as stress, health issues, or personal challenges.
The available information suggests that a conversation would be useful.
The evidence supports concern, but it does not yet prove the reason behind the behaviour.
revisedInterpretation: Something appears to have changed, but I do not know the cause. It is worth discussing openly rather than assuming the relationship is ending.
chosenBehaviour: Have a calm and direct conversation about the changes I have noticed.
outcomeOneWeekLater: My partner explained they had been dealing with significant work stress and appreciated the discussion.

event: My partner frequently checks their phone during conversations with me.
rawInterpretation: They find me boring and would rather be talking to other people.
alternateRealityChecks: Phone use has become a common habit for many people.
The behaviour may be caused by habit or distraction rather than lack of interest.
Your frustration is understandable because the behaviour affects connection.
Regardless of intent, discussing how the behaviour impacts you may be helpful.
revisedInterpretation: The phone use may not mean they find me boring, but it is a behaviour worth discussing because it affects how connected I feel.
chosenBehaviour: Explain how the behaviour affects me rather than assuming intent.
outcomeOneWeekLater: My partner was unaware of the impact and agreed to be more present during conversations.

event: I noticed that my partner has recently become very protective of their phone and online activity.
rawInterpretation: They must be hiding something from me.
alternateRealityChecks: People sometimes increase privacy for reasons unrelated to infidelity or dishonesty.
Changes in behaviour can have multiple explanations.
However, the change is noticeable and it is reasonable to be curious about it.
Additional information is needed before reaching conclusions.
revisedInterpretation: The behavioural change is worth discussing, but I do not have enough evidence to know what it means.
chosenBehaviour: Approach the topic with curiosity instead of accusation.
outcomeOneWeekLater: The behaviour was related to planning a surprise birthday event.

event: My partner has forgotten several commitments they made to me over the past month.
rawInterpretation: They do not respect me or my needs.
alternateRealityChecks: Repeated missed commitments can be a legitimate concern.
The behaviour may reflect stress, disorganisation, or competing priorities rather than lack of respect.
Patterns are worth discussing directly.
The evidence supports addressing the issue but not assuming the underlying motive.
revisedInterpretation: There seems to be a recurring issue that needs discussion, but I cannot know the reason without talking about it.
chosenBehaviour: Discuss the pattern and its impact on the relationship.
outcomeOneWeekLater: We agreed on ways to better manage commitments and expectations.

event: My partner openly shared that they have been feeling unhappy in the relationship recently.
alternateRealityChecks: This is important information that deserves attention.
Expressing unhappiness does not automatically mean someone wants to end the relationship.
Many relationships experience periods of dissatisfaction that can be addressed together.
The discussion signals a problem that requires effort, not necessarily an unavoidable ending.
revisedInterpretation: There is a genuine issue that needs attention, but the future of the relationship has not been determined.
chosenBehaviour: Explore the concerns together and identify possible improvements.
outcomeOneWeekLater: Both partners agreed to work on communication and spend more intentional time together.
